slides.headline: Airlines Oversell. Your Rights Have Limits.
slides.subheadline: The no-show gamble makes compensation conditional—not overselling illegal.
slides.svgBlueprint: viewBox='0 0 952 650'. Build a monumental three-quarter airplane-seat specimen centered at (490,325), bounded by x=310–735 and y=48–594. Two oversized, opposing boarding passes approach the same cushion: left pass within x=42–383, y=172–350, rotated −12 degrees; right pass within x=627–906, y=100–278, rotated 12 degrees. Both carry the fictional seat label '12A'. Orange trajectories converge at the cushion without implying that either passenger has already boarded. Print only '$0', '200%' and '400%' on this teaser plate; the complete eligibility and cap schedule appears on slide 5. Construct at least 60 primitives, including variable-width illustrative barcode stripes measuring 1–5px. Clip those stripes inside the pass stock, not across typography. Keep all transformed corners inside a 24px SVG inset.

slides.headline: Too Many Passengers Show Up
slides.subheadline: Airlines must seek volunteers before forcing anyone off.

items.title: YOUR LEVERAGE
items.body: **Uncapped negotiation**; require compensation and voucher disclosures.

items.title: YOUR CHECKLIST
items.body: Confirm **replacement seat**, meals, hotel, transfers, voucher restrictions.

slides.footer: Check voucher expiration, holiday restrictions, international usability.
slides.svgBlueprint: viewBox='0 0 952 420'. Draw a continuous gate-counter assembly rather than separate icons. At x=50–310, two overlapping boarding passes feed toward a scanner at (365,205). The boarding lane continues toward a detailed seat at x=735–887, y=100–344, but a hinged mechanical gate at x=690 remains closed until the volunteer stage is considered. A tall voucher specimen links visually to the larger left HTML card; a luggage-tag-shaped checklist specimen links to the narrower right card. Construct at least 55 primitives. Add labels '01' and '02' at the branch junctions; explain their meaning in HTML.

slides.headline: Losing Your Seat Isn't Enough
slides.subheadline: Involuntary compensation requires these conditions, subject to exclusions.

items.title: PASSENGER REQUIREMENTS
items.body: Confirmed reservation; **timely check-in and gate arrival**.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use two coordinated SVGs, each viewBox='0 0 448 420', rendered side by side in 448px columns separated by 56px. Left: a boarding pass mounted in a gate-validation cradle at x=44–400, y=72–320. Its notched paper body, barcode and three inspection anchors correspond to reservation, check-in and gate arrival. A clock at (338,94), radius 54, represents timeliness without inventing a universal check-in deadline. Right: an aircraft-window-shaped inspection plate at x=38–410, y=28–390. A technical airplane profile crosses a U.S.-departure origin marker and ends beside a destination clock at (300,255), radius 86. Add the anchored label '>1 h' and a separate open eligibility latch; do not use a green approval badge or imply these checks override exclusions. Connect both specimens across the gutter with one HTML-positioned hairline and an AND label. Draw at least 35 primitives in each SVG.

slides.headline: Operational Exceptions Block Compensation Claims

items.title: OPERATIONAL EXCLUSIONS
items.body: **Operational/safety** smaller-aircraft substitutions; weight/balance restrictions, aircraft ≤60 seats.

items.title: EXCLUDED FLIGHTS
items.body: **Charters, foreign departures**, scheduled aircraft below 30 seats.

slides.svgBlueprint: viewBox='0 0 952 420'. Run a double technical release rail from (44,240) to (908,240). At x=100–335, show a larger aircraft cabin section above a smaller replacement section, connected by a downward exchange arrow and an interrupted authorization gate. At x=370–625, show a compact aircraft fuselage on a load-and-balance inspection rig: wing spar, paired load points, center-of-gravity crosshair and a dimension bracket labeled '≤60 seats'. At x=674–900, show a departure-document stack beside a compact cabin cross-section labeled '<30 seats'; a globe-origin ring identifies the foreign-departure exclusion without implying those flights have no rights under other laws. Three orange physical stop tabs intersect the rail. Number the stations 01–03 and map their meanings in HTML. Draw at least 65 primitives; cabin seat modules indicate aircraft anatomy, not literal seat counts.

slides.headline: Delay Turns Displacement Into Cash
slides.subheadline: Eligible involuntary bumping: percentages apply to one-way fares.
slides.footer: International: U.S. departures. Airlines may pay more.
slides.svgBlueprint: viewBox='0 0 952 420'. Enlarge the cover seat's armrest into a top-down technical specimen spanning x=88–864, y=30–390. Show its rounded outer molding, recessed compensation plate, side release button, pivot bracket and exposed mounting screws. The inset plate contains a continuous vertical milestone spine at x=210, y=104–334, with three anchored nodes at y=120, 220 and 320. At x=278–815, bevel three populated milestone panels into the plate. Panel 1: '$0' and '≤1 h'. Panel 2: '200%', 'CAP $1,075', 'D: 1<h<2', 'I: 1<h<4'. Panel 3: '400%', 'CAP $2,150', 'D: h≥2', 'I: h≥4'. Use 34px percentage labels and 23px range labels. SVG contains only these anchored numerical labels; explain D, I and h directly below in HTML. Preserve all three tiers at equal physical panel heights: this is a schedule, not a magnitude chart. Draw at least 45 primitives.

slides.headline: Rare Doesn't Mean It Disappears
slides.subheadline: Fourth quarter 2024; 10 U.S. reporting marketing carriers.
slides.footer: Bumping frequency—not the percentage of tickets oversold.

slides.headline: Know Which Deal You're Taking
slides.subheadline: A negotiated surrender isn't an automatic cash entitlement.

items.title: VOLUNTEER DEAL
items.body: Trade your seat only for **acceptable terms**.

items.title: ELIGIBLE INVOLUNTARY
items.body: **Cash or immediately negotiable check**, same-day, same-place.

slides.footer: Replacement departs before payment? Deadline: **24 hours**.
slides.svgBlueprint: viewBox='0 0 952 420'. Resolve the cover's competing-pass motif with a mechanical sorting rail, not a moral good/bad split. The upper route ends in a perforated negotiated-voucher specimen at x=456–878, y=32–178; the lower ends in an immediately negotiable check specimen at x=456–878, y=224–372. Use equally legible ink outlines for both artifacts. Orange emphasizes the selector and the payment timing exception, not one passenger's superiority.
